metadata.description: Gesture Recognition Dataset with Subclips (Synced from Frontend)

classes.name: machine
classes.description: The gesture begins with the right hand placed flat on the upper left chest, fingers held together and thumb tucked. From this initial position, the hand extends directly forward and slightly downwards in a linear motion, partially extending the arm with the palm generally facing forward or downwards. Immediately after the forward extension, the hand retracts to its original position on the upper left chest. This full sequence of forward extension and return is repeated several times. A distinctive feature is the repetitive, piston-like linear movement from the chest without any complex finger articulation or rotational elements often associated with machinery. The accompanying audio repeatedly features a voice speaking the French word "Null".

classes.name: loop
classes.description: The "loop" gesture involves a continuous, gentle rocking motion of the upper body, primarily the torso and head. The person begins slightly bent forward with their head down, hands loosely touching their thighs. They then smoothly sway their upper body backward to a more upright position, tilting the head up, before returning to the initial bent-forward, head-down pose, creating a repetitive, fluid, cyclical motion. The hands remain passive, lightly resting or following the slight movement of the thighs. This body movement is distinctly synchronized with a rhythmic vocalization or sound effect that sounds like "ding-ah-ah," repeating continuously with each rock.

classes.name: cest_nul
classes.description: The gesture begins with both hands raised to approximately chest height, palms facing forward, and thumbs pointing upwards. Simultaneously, both hands rotate at the wrists, moving downwards until the thumbs point downwards, signifying disapproval. This action is accompanied by the spoken word "Nul," which is French for "worthless" or "bad."

classes.name: drum
classes.description: The "drum" gesture begins with both hands clenched into fists and held in front of the body, approximately at chest or abdomen height, with elbows bent. From this initial position, both fists move rhythmically and synchronously up and down in short, quick, repetitive arcs, mimicking the action of drumming. There is no distinct final position as the gesture is a continuous, repetitive motion. Key distinguishing features include the use of both hands in a fist shape, their synchronized and repetitive up-and-down movement, and the crucial accompaniment of a rapid, rhythmic drumming sound effect synchronized with each beat.

classes.name: navigue
classes.description: The "navigue" gesture begins with the individual standing upright, raising both hands to eye level. Each hand forms a loose fist with the index finger extended. The tips of the extended index fingers are placed near the temples, just above the outer corners of the eyes, creating a visual impression of holding binoculars or goggles. The gesture involves a subtle, continuous rhythmic "wiggling" or "swiveling" motion of the index fingers at the temples, suggesting an active visual scan or navigation. This movement is consistently accompanied by a distinctive, repeated "ooh-ooh" sound, akin to a pigeon's coo, synchronized with the visual action.
